verdict.rationale: Factory documents `droid exec` as a headless, one-shot mode built for CI/CD pipelines, with structured input/output and tiered autonomy, so an agent can clearly be triggered from a pipeline. However, nothing in the pack documents a workflow for detecting a broken build or failing test and having Droid fix it; the evidence only covers general task execution and PR code review in CI. missing for 10: documented CI-failure-to-fix workflow (e.g., triggering on a failed build or test job and pushing a fix), examples or integrations for specific CI providers, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trigger an agent from CI/CD pipelines to fix a broken build or failing test

citations.quote: Droid Exec is Factory's headless execution mode designed for automation workflows. Unlike the interactive CLI, `droid exec` runs as a one-shot command that completes a task and exits, making it ideal for CI/CD pipelines, shell scripts, and batch processing.
droid exec runs in scripts and CI/CD pipelines with structured input and output formats.
Droid exec uses tiered autonomy to control what operations can run without manual confirmation.
